title: Smoothness at a finite type point detected by completed local formal smoothness
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $B$ be a finite type commutative $R$-algebra, meaning generated as an $R$-algebra by finitely many elements. Let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be a prime ideal with inverse image $\mathfrak m_R$, and let $C=\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q}}=\varprojlim_nB_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q})^n$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth on an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if $R\to C$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: Tag 07VH, lemma-formally-smooth-finite-type, and Tag 07ED, lemma-formally-smooth-completion, equivalence (1) and (2).

proof.text: Put $T=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qT$. The localization definition gives that $T$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], $B$ and $T$ are Noetherian. Thus $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $\iota:T\to C$ for completion. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $C$ is local and $\mathfrak m_C=\mathfrak nC$. In particular the topology in the conclusion is exactly the extended-ideal topology used in the completion lemmas.

Assume the smooth-neighbourhood condition: there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\mathfrak q\in W$ and $\pi|_W:W\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ smooth, where $\pi=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to B)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (i) there is $g\in B$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(g)\subseteq W$, so $g\notin\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] (a), applied to $\pi|_W$, the open subscheme $D(g)$ of $W$ and the open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the target, the restriction $p:D(g)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ induced by $B\to B_g$ is an open immersion with image $D(g)$, so by [def-weil-open-immersion] $j$ is an isomorphism $\sigma:\operatorname{Spec}B_g\xrightarrow{\sim}D(g)$ followed by the inclusion of the open subscheme $D(g)$. Then $p\circ\sigma=\pi\circ j=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to B\to B_g)$ by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], with the isomorphism $\sigma$ and the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, shows that $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to B_g)$ is smooth, and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] shows that $R\to B_g$ is a smooth ring map.

source.place: Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize) with Algebra Tag 00TB (definition-smooth-at-prime): the identification of a smooth open neighbourhood with smoothness of R -> B_g at q used in Tag 07VH (lemma-formally-smooth-finite-type), proof of (1) implies (2); comparison of the two smoothness notions by more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth).

proof.text: Keep $g$ from step 2, so $R\to B_g$ is a smooth ring map. We check adic lifting for $R\to T$. Given an $R$-algebra $D$, a square-zero ideal $J$, and $u:T\to D/J$, restrict $u$ to $B_g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-square-zero-lifting] it lifts to $v:B_g\to D$. The ring $T$ is a localization of $B_g$ at the images of $B\setminus\mathfrak q$: fractions in $B_g$ have denominators powers of $g$, already invertible in $T$, and subsequently inverting those images gives precisely the fractions defining $T$. Give $D$ its $B_g$-algebra structure through $v$ and use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting] to lift $u$ to $T\to D$ over $B_g$, hence over $R$. This works for every $u$, in particular those killing a power of $\mathfrak n$, and proves [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $R\to T$.

source.place: Tag 07VH (lemma-formally-smooth-finite-type), proof of (1) implies (2), with the localization lifting argument written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-completion] to $R\to T$ and its finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak n$ from step 1. It gives adic formal smoothness of $R\to C$ for $\mathfrak nC=\mathfrak m_C$. This proves the forward implication.

Conversely assume $R\to C$ is formally smooth for $\mathfrak m_C$. Consider any small-extension test $a:B\to A$, $\rho:R\to A'$, $e:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ in condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-artinian-lifting]. Thus $A',A$ are Artinian local, $\ker e$ has length one, $a^{-1}(\mathfrak m_A)=\mathfrak q$, and $a\circ(R\to B)=e\rho$. For $s\notin\mathfrak q$, $a(s)\notin\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit, so fractions define $a_T:T\to A$. Elements of $\mathfrak n$ map into $\mathfrak m_A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] choose $N\geq1$ with $\mathfrak m_A^N=0$. Thus $a_T$ factors through a map $\bar a:T/\mathfrak n^N\to A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], the coordinate projection $\pi_N:C\twoheadrightarrow T/\mathfrak n^N$ has kernel $\mathfrak n^NC=\mathfrak m_C^N$ and satisfies $\pi_N\iota(t)=t\bmod\mathfrak n^N$. Hence $\widetilde a=\bar a\pi_N:C\to A$ is an $R$-algebra map killing $\mathfrak m_C^N$, and $\widetilde a\iota=a_T$.

source.place: Tag 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), proof via the finite quotients; Tag 07VH (lemma-formally-smooth-finite-type), (2) implies (1).

proof.text: Set $J=\ker e$. It has square zero: a length-one ideal is a simple $A'$-module, so $\mathfrak m_{A'}J=0$; also $J\subset\mathfrak m_{A'}$ since the nonzero quotient $A$ is local. Consequently $J^2=0$. Identify $A'/J$ with $A$ by the surjection $e$. Apply the assumed lifting property [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] to $\widetilde a:C\to A'/J$ from step 5. It gives an $R$-algebra map $h:C\to A'$ with $eh=\widetilde a$. The composite $B\to T\xrightarrow{\iota}C\xrightarrow{h}A'$ is the required lift: its composite with $e$ is $a$, and its composite with $R\to B$ is $\rho$ because every map used is an $R$-algebra map. Every small-extension test therefore lifts. Condition (2) implies condition (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-at-prime-artinian-lifting], giving precisely the asserted smooth open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$.
